holidays.name: National Deep Dish Pizza Day
holidays.description: A day for knife-and-fork pizza lovers. It honors the thick, buttery-crusted, sauce-on-top pie that is more casserole than flatbread. Grab a fork, loosen your belt, and settle in for a slice that takes real commitment.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial food-calendar observance. It celebrates the pan-baked pizza style that was created in Chicago in 1943.
holidays.funFact: Chicago deep dish is usually built upside down compared with other pizzas, with the cheese on the bottom and the chunky tomato sauce on top. Baking a real one can take 30 to 45 minutes.

holidays.name: National Dandelion Day
holidays.description: A cheerful defense of the lawn's most hated yellow guest. Put down the weed killer and take a fresh look at the plant. Its leaves can go in salads, its blooms can be made into wine, and its flowers make crowns and bouquets.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It arrives each spring, when dandelions are among the first flowers many pollinators can find.
holidays.funFact: The name comes from the French "dent de lion," meaning lion's tooth, a nod to the plant's jagged, toothy leaves.

holidays.name: Bell Bottoms Day
holidays.description: A day to flare up your wardrobe. Pull on your widest, swishiest trousers and bring some 1970s groove to the day. The flare is optional only in the sense that more is better.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial pop-culture observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the pants whose legs widen dramatically below the knee.
holidays.funFact: Bell-bottoms are strongly linked to 1960s and 70s fashion. Their roots go back much further, to sailors' trousers, whose wide legs were easy to roll up and quick to kick off.
